name: An Amalekite reports Saul and Jonathan's deaths and is executed
summary: A messenger claims to have killed the wounded Saul at Mount Gilboa, and David has him executed for killing the LORD's anointed.

name: David composes a lament for Saul and Jonathan
summary: David sings a lament called the Song of the Bow, mourning Saul and Jonathan together and celebrating the bond he shared with Jonathan.

name: David is anointed king over the tribe of Judah
summary: David inquires of the LORD, moves to Hebron, and is anointed king over Judah, while Abner makes Saul's son Ish-bosheth king over the rest of Israel.

name: Abner's men clash with Joab's men and Asahel is killed
summary: Twelve men from each side fight to the death at the pool of Gibeon, then Abner kills Joab's brother Asahel during the retreat, fueling a long war between the two houses.

name: Abner quarrels with Ish-bosheth and defects to David
summary: After Ish-bosheth accuses him of taking Saul's concubine Rizpah, an insulted Abner offers to bring all of Israel over to David's side.

name: Joab murders Abner in revenge for Asahel
summary: Joab lures Abner aside and stabs him to death, avenging his brother Asahel but wrecking David's fragile peace with the rest of Israel.

name: David publicly mourns Abner and curses Joab's house
summary: David walks behind Abner's funeral bier weeping, declares his own innocence in the killing, and pronounces a curse on Joab's family for the murder.

name: Rechab and Baanah murder Ish-bosheth in his bed
summary: Two of Ish-bosheth's own captains sneak into his house while he naps, kill him, and carry his head to David expecting a reward.

name: David executes Ish-bosheth's murderers
summary: David condemns the two captains for killing an innocent man in his own house, has them executed, and buries Ish-bosheth's head in Abner's tomb.

name: All Israel anoints David king over the whole nation
summary: The elders of all the tribes come and anoint David king over the whole nation, seven years after he became king over Judah alone.

name: David captures the Jebusite stronghold and makes it his capital
summary: David's men take the fortress the Jebusites had called unconquerable, and David builds it up as his new capital, known as the City of David.

name: David defeats the Philistines twice
summary: The Philistines attack the new king twice, and both times David inquires of the LORD first and routs them in the valley of Rephaim.

name: Uzzah touches the ark and dies
summary: As the ark is carried toward Jerusalem on a new cart, Uzzah reaches out to steady it and is struck dead, and a frightened David halts the procession.

name: David brings the ark into the city with dancing and celebration
summary: Three months later David leads the ark in with sacrifices, music, and dancing, wearing a simple linen ephod in front of the whole procession.

name: Michal despises David and is confronted for it
summary: Watching from a window, Michal despises David for dancing before the people, and when he returns home she mocks him, and he sharply rebukes her in reply.

name: David proposes building God a house and Nathan first agrees
summary: David tells the prophet Nathan he wants to build a permanent house for the ark, and Nathan tells him to go ahead with whatever is on his heart.

name: Nathan delivers God's covenant promise of an everlasting dynasty
summary: That same night the LORD tells Nathan that David will not build God a house, but instead God will build David a house, an everlasting royal dynasty.

name: David wins a series of military victories
summary: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, the king of Zobah, the Arameans, and Edom, dedicating the plunder and tribute from these campaigns to the LORD.

name: David appoints officials over his kingdom
summary: A summary list names Joab as army commander and other officials over David's priests, recorders, scribes, and bodyguard as his kingdom is established.

name: David learns that Jonathan's son Mephibosheth is still alive
summary: For Jonathan's sake, David asks if anyone from Saul's house is left, and Saul's servant Ziba tells him that Jonathan's crippled son is living there.

name: David restores Mephibosheth's land and gives him a place at his table
summary: David returns all of Saul's former land to Mephibosheth, assigns Ziba to farm it for him, and has Mephibosheth eat at the king's table from then on.

name: Hanun humiliates David's envoys of comfort
summary: When David sends men to console the new Ammonite king Hanun over his father's death, Hanun's advisors convince him to shave off half their beards and cut off their garments.

name: Joab and Abishai defeat the Ammonite-Aramean coalition
summary: The humiliated Ammonites hire Aramean mercenaries, but Joab and his brother Abishai split their forces and rout both armies, and David later defeats the reinforcements himself.

name: David sees Bathsheba and sends for her
place: the roof of the king's house
summary: While his army is off at war, David stays behind in the city, sees Bathsheba bathing, sends for her, and sleeps with her, and she conceives.

name: Uriah refuses to go home while his fellow soldiers are at war
summary: David recalls Bathsheba's husband Uriah from the battle hoping he will sleep with his wife and cover the pregnancy, but Uriah sleeps at the palace door out of loyalty to his fellow soldiers.

name: David arranges for Uriah to be killed in battle
summary: David sends Uriah back to the front carrying his own death sentence, and Joab positions him where the fighting is fiercest so that he is killed.

name: Nathan confronts David with a parable and says 'You are the man'
summary: Nathan tells David a story about a rich man stealing a poor man's only lamb, and when David condemns the man in anger, Nathan tells him he is that man.

name: The child born to Bathsheba dies despite David's pleading
summary: David fasts and pleads with God for seven days as the child grows sick, but the boy dies, and David surprises his servants by rising to worship instead of mourning.

name: Solomon is born and David finishes off the Ammonites
summary: The LORD blesses David and Bathsheba's next son Solomon, and David completes the Ammonite campaign by capturing the enemy capital and taking its king's crown.

name: Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar
summary: Amnon fakes illness to get Tamar alone, and despite her pleading he forces himself on her, then hates her and has her thrown out of his house.

name: Absalom has Amnon killed at a sheep-shearing feast
summary: Two years later Absalom invites all the king's sons to a feast and orders his servants to kill Amnon once he is drunk with wine.

name: Absalom flees to his grandfather's kingdom
summary: Absalom escapes to where his mother's father is king and stays there three years while David mourns the loss of both of his sons.

name: A wise woman persuades David to allow Absalom's return
summary: Joab sends a wise woman to tell David a fictional story about her own sons, leading the king to see that he should bring his banished son home.

name: Absalom returns to Jerusalem but is later reconciled with David
summary: David allows Absalom back but refuses to see him for two years, until Absalom burns Joab's field to force a meeting that ends with father and son reconciled.

name: Absalom wins over the hearts of the people of Israel
summary: For four years Absalom rises early to intercept people bringing disputes to the king, telling them their case is right but that no one will hear them.

name: Absalom has himself proclaimed king
summary: Absalom asks David's permission to go and worship, then has himself proclaimed king there, and the conspiracy against David grows strong very quickly.

name: David flees Jerusalem and sends Hushai back as a spy
summary: David leaves the city weeping, and the foreigner Ittai pledges to stay with him no matter what, while Hushai returns to counter Ahithophel's advice.

name: Ziba deceives David about Mephibosheth's loyalty
summary: Ziba meets the fleeing David with supplies and falsely claims Mephibosheth hopes the rebellion will restore Saul's kingdom to him, so David gives Ziba all of Mephibosheth's property.

name: Shimei curses David and throws stones along the road
summary: A man from Saul's family named Shimei curses David and pelts him with stones, and David restrains one of his men from killing him for it.

name: Absalom publicly takes David's concubines on Ahithophel's advice
summary: On Ahithophel's counsel, Absalom sleeps with David's concubines on the palace roof in front of all Israel, a public act meant to seal the break with his father.

name: Ahithophel and Hushai give Absalom opposing counsel
summary: Ahithophel urges an immediate strike against the exhausted David, but Hushai argues for delay to gather all Israel first, and Absalom chooses Hushai's advice.

name: Hushai's warning reaches David and Ahithophel hangs himself
summary: Messengers hide in a well to carry Hushai's warning to David, and Ahithophel, seeing his counsel rejected, goes home, sets his affairs in order, and hangs himself.

name: David crosses the Jordan and reaches safety
summary: David and his people cross the Jordan River during the night and take refuge there, where local leaders bring supplies for his weary men.

name: David's army defeats Absalom's forces
summary: David sends his troops out under three commanders but stays behind himself, and his forces defeat Absalom's army decisively.

name: Absalom's head catches in a tree and Joab kills him
summary: As Absalom flees on his mule, his head gets caught in the branches of a tree, and Joab kills him with three javelins despite David's order to spare his life.

name: David mourns deeply for Absalom
summary: When runners bring word of Absalom's death, David goes up to his room weeping and crying out that he wishes he had died instead of his son.

name: Joab rebukes David for mourning instead of thanking his troops
summary: Joab tells David his grief has turned a great victory into shame and warns that the army will desert him unless he goes out to encourage them at once.

name: David pardons Shimei and divides Mephibosheth's land with Ziba
summary: As David crosses back over, he spares Shimei's life, hears Mephibosheth's side of Ziba's earlier lie, and splits the disputed land between the two of them.

name: Barzillai is honored and Israel and Judah argue over David
summary: David thanks the elderly Barzillai for supplying him in exile, and a sharp argument breaks out between Israel and Judah over who has the greater claim to the king.

name: Sheba leads Israel in revolt against David
summary: A Benjaminite named Sheba blows a trumpet and calls all of Israel away from David, splitting the kingdom again just as the rebellion with Absalom ends.

name: Joab kills Amasa and the revolt ends
summary: Joab treacherously kills the new commander Amasa, then chases Sheba to a walled city, where a wise woman convinces the people to end the siege by throwing his head over the wall.

name: David hands over seven of Saul's descendants to the Gibeonites
summary: To end a three-year famine caused by Saul's bloodguilt against the Gibeonites, David hands over seven of Saul's descendants for execution, and Rizpah guards their bodies before David buries the remains with Saul and Jonathan's bones.

name: David's men kill four Philistine giants
summary: In renewed fighting with the Philistines, David's men kill four descendants of the giant Rapha, including a brother of Goliath, after David himself grows faint in battle.

name: David sings a song of deliverance to the LORD
summary: David sings a long song praising God as his rock, fortress, and deliverer, recounting how the LORD rescued him from Saul and from all his other enemies.

name: David's last words describe the ideal, righteous ruler
summary: In his final recorded words, David describes a ruler who governs in the fear of God as being like the light of morning, and recalls God's everlasting covenant with his house.

name: A roster of David's mighty men lists their exploits
summary: A list of David's elite warriors and their feats includes three men who broke through Philistine lines to bring David water from a well, which he poured out to the LORD instead of drinking.

name: David orders a census despite Joab's objection, and a plague follows
summary: David orders Joab to count the fighting men of Israel and Judah, and after Joab reluctantly complies, God gives David a choice of three punishments and sends a plague that kills seventy thousand people.

name: David insists on paying full price to build an altar
summary: On Gad's instruction David refuses a free gift and buys a Jebusite's plot of land at full price, builds an altar there, and the plague stops after he offers sacrifices.
